Week of November 23, 2026

DNC Schedules 12 Debates With a Dark-Money Pledge as Ossoff Tops a National Poll Despite Saying He Won't Run

The Democratic National Committee set the rules of the road for 2028 on November 23. It will hold 12 primary debates, five in 2027, the first two in June and July, and seven in 2028, six of them in the early-voting states. Debates may be split across two nights with no more than 20 qualifying candidates, chosen by polling and grassroots fundraising. Candidates must also sign a pledge to denounce super PAC and dark-money spending that boosts them or attacks a Democratic rival, a largely symbolic rule the party cannot force outside groups to obey. Dates and media partners for the first two debates will be announced in January.

Nobody declared this week, but the groundwork continued. Allies of Pete Buttigieg launched Team Pete PAC to urge him to run, Cory Booker made his fourth South Carolina trip of the year and told reporters he is giving a run a lot of thought, and Gavin Newsom spent several days in Washington pitching AI regulation as an issue no 2028 candidate can ignore. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez filed paperwork for a House re-election bid, which does not settle her choice, and said Democrats should focus on getting results. Sen. Bernie Sanders, 85, said he probably will not run.

An Emerson College poll taken November 14 to 16 put Jon Ossoff first among Democratic primary voters at 17 percent, narrowly ahead of Kamala Harris at 16, Ocasio-Cortez at 15 and Buttigieg at 14, with Newsom at 11. Ossoff still says he is not running, so we hold him at 8. Odds moves are small: Booker rises a point to 3 on his South Carolina push, and Newsom slips a point to 11 as his polling has fallen from the mid-20s early this year to the low teens. The unlisted field holds at 15 percent.

    DNC sets 2028 debate rules

    The Democratic National Committee announced 12 primary debates, five in 2027 beginning in June and seven in 2028, six of them in early-voting states. Up to 20 candidates may qualify across two nights based on polling and grassroots fundraising, and each must sign a pledge to denounce super PAC and dark-money spending in the primary. Source

  • Nov 7, 2026
    Crooked Con straw poll

    Jon Ossoff was the first choice of 38.4 percent of 990 attendees at Crooked Media's progressive conference, followed by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at 16.6 percent and Pete Buttigieg at about 14 percent. It is an unscientific poll of activists. Source

  • Nov 3, 2026
    2026 midterm elections

    Democrats won control of the House and Senate and a majority of governorships. As of November 10 they had flipped at least seven Senate seats, including Texas, Ohio and North Carolina, with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled along with 19 House races. Source

  • Nov 3, 2026
    Illinois governor

    JB Pritzker defeated Republican Darren Bailey to win a third term. Source

  • Aug 15, 2026
    DNC approves 2028 nominating calendar

    The full Democratic National Committee approved by voice vote a calendar that puts South Carolina first, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia. States that go out of order lose all of their delegates and face a $270,000 fine. Source

The Hopefuls

#1 12%

Kamala Harris

Former Vice President of the United States

Undeclared

Background

Harris was California attorney general, a U.S. senator, and vice president from 2021 to 2025. She was the Democratic nominee in 2024. She declined to run for governor of California in 2026 and campaigned for Democrats in the midterms.

Outlook

Harris leads the national polling averages, and Emerson's mid-November poll had her second at 16 percent in a closed list, a point behind Ossoff. Prediction markets put her near 5 percent, and she finished far back in the Crooked Con activist straw poll. She has not decided, and Newsom's pledge not to run against her means her choice shapes the whole field.

  • A CNN/SSRS poll found Harris, Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg drew the most excitement among Democrats, though Harris also had the largest share who said they would never back her. CNN, Nov 11, 2026

#2 11%

Gavin Newsom

Governor of California (term ends January 2027)

Undeclared

Background

Newsom was mayor of San Francisco and lieutenant governor before becoming governor in 2019. He is term-limited and leaves office in January 2027. He has built a national profile through confrontations with President Trump and a redistricting push in California.

Outlook

Down one point. Newsom has a firm decision date, early January, and a clear public condition: he says he would not run against Harris. His trip to Washington this week to promote AI regulation looked like groundwork for a campaign, but one polling average shows his support among Democrats sliding from 25 percent in January to 13 percent, and he drew 11 percent in Emerson's November poll, behind Ossoff, Harris, Ocasio-Cortez and Buttigieg.

  • Newsom told Turkey's Anadolu news agency he will decide on a 2028 run in early January, after time with his family. Fox News via Yahoo News, Nov 13, 2026
  • Newsom told CNN he would not run if Harris does, calling a contest between the two California Democrats mutually destructive. The National News Desk via FOX 11, Sep 15, 2026

In Their Words

#3 11%

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

U.S. Representative from New York

Undeclared

Background

Ocasio-Cortez has represented parts of the Bronx and Queens since 2019. She toured the country with Sen. Bernie Sanders in 2025 and has become one of the best-known progressives in the party.

Outlook

She has said she would decide after the midterms between a presidential run and a Senate challenge to Chuck Schumer, and she has not announced a choice. She filed paperwork for a House re-election bid, which keeps that option open without ruling out the others. She polled 15 percent in Emerson's November survey and second in prediction markets near 15 percent, but a Senate run remains a lower-risk path, which holds her odds below the top tier.

#4 10%

Pete Buttigieg

Former U.S. Secretary of Transportation

Undeclared

Background

Buttigieg was mayor of South Bend, Indiana, and finished among the top candidates in the 2020 Democratic primary. He served as Transportation Secretary from 2021 to 2025.

Outlook

Buttigieg has said he leans toward running but will not announce anything soon. Former aides launched Team Pete PAC this week to urge him in, and he drew 14 percent in Emerson's November poll, fourth in a tight top group. Prediction markets price him near 5 percent, reflecting doubts about his support among Black voters ahead of a calendar that opens in South Carolina.

#5 9%

Josh Shapiro

Governor of Pennsylvania

Undeclared

Background

Shapiro was Pennsylvania attorney general before winning the governorship in 2022. He was on Kamala Harris's vice presidential shortlist in 2024 and was re-elected on November 3, 2026.

Outlook

Up one point. Shapiro followed his decisive re-election with a campaign-style speech in Denver, and CNN reports that he is expected to launch a bid. He says the timing is a family decision and will not commit yet. National polls have him in the mid single digits and many Democrats still do not know him, but his swing-state record makes him the strongest governor in the field on paper.

#6 8%

Jon Ossoff

U.S. Senator from Georgia

Undeclared

Background

Jon Ossoff has represented Georgia in the U.S. Senate since 2021 and won a second term on November 3, 2026. A former investigative journalist, he is the youngest sitting Democratic senator.

Outlook

Ossoff topped Emerson's November national poll at 17 percent, ranks first in prediction markets and won the Crooked Con straw poll. But he has said repeatedly that he is not running and pledged at an October debate to serve his full six-year term. We take the pledge seriously and hold him well below his polling and market price, but a swing-state winner this popular with the party stays on the board until the field is set.

  • Asked at a Georgia Senate debate whether he would serve a full term, Ossoff said yes and repeated that he is not running for president. Fox News, Oct 14, 2026

#7 6%

JB Pritzker

Governor of Illinois

Undeclared

Background

Pritzker, a billionaire and heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, has been governor of Illinois since 2019. He has been a leading Democratic critic of President Trump and has funded abortion-rights and other Democratic causes.

Outlook

Pritzker won a third term on November 3, the first Illinois governor to do so since 1982, and told supporters they were at the base of another mountain. He has not ruled out a run. Wealth gives him a financial advantage, though his profile outside Illinois is thinner than that of the top contenders.

Andy Beshear

Governor of Kentucky

Undeclared

Background

Beshear was Kentucky attorney general before winning the governorship in 2019 and was re-elected in 2023, both times in a state that voted heavily for Donald Trump. He chairs the Democratic Governors Association.

Outlook

Beshear has said he is considering a run, has pitched Democratic governors as the party's face, and has held early talks with potential campaign staff, according to the Associated Press. Prediction markets price him around 4 percent. His red-state record is his main argument. He has not set a date for a decision.

Mark Kelly

U.S. Senator from Arizona

Undeclared

Background

Kelly is a retired Navy captain and former astronaut who has represented Arizona in the Senate since 2020. He drew national attention after the Pentagon moved to demote him over a video urging service members to refuse illegal orders, and he sued Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over it.

Outlook

Kelly said he would not decide until after the midterms, and the Associated Press reports he has already talked with potential campaign staff. He polls in the mid single digits, and 22 percent of Democrats in the CNN/SSRS poll said they would be excited to back him. His military record and his clash with the administration are assets, but he lacks a large national base.

Background

Khanna has represented a Silicon Valley district since 2017 and was a national co-chair of Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaign. He has built a profile on economic nationalism, Medicare for All and opposition to foreign wars.

Progressives are not unified behind him, and he competes for the same lane as Ocasio-Cortez.

U.S. Senator from New Jersey

Undeclared

Background

Booker was mayor of Newark before winning a Senate seat in 2013, and he ran for the Democratic presidential nomination in 2020. He won re-election to a third full term on November 3, 2026.

Booker made his fourth South Carolina trip of the year, keynoting the Charleston NAACP gala and visiting Mother Emanuel, and told reporters afterward he is giving a run a lot of thought. South Carolina votes first, and he starts with more than $20 million in his federal campaign account. His 2020 campaign ended before the first votes, and prediction markets give him under 1 percent.

About This Tracker

Project 2028 is researched and written each week by an AI model (Anthropic's Claude), which reads current reporting, polling, and public statements, then rebuilds this page. The odds are the model's own judgment of who wins the Democratic nomination. They are not a poll, a betting market, or an endorsement, and they will be wrong in interesting ways.

Headlines and quotes link to their sources. If something here is inaccurate, the linked source is the authority.

Last updated November 23, 2026. Independent and unaffiliated with any candidate, campaign, or party.
